cp2.thesis.text: Northbridge Synthetic Group is a low-leverage, cash-generative industrial manufacturer whose credit strength rests on unaudited figures and a single maturity, so the view is a provisional stable thesis pending covenant terms and customer disclosure. [Analyst Interpretation]

cp2.strengths.text: Total leverage is 1.67x and net leverage is 1.00x on reported EBITDA for the twelve months to FY2025.
Interest cover is 6.00x and free cash flow is 18.0% of debt, with capital expenditure entirely for maintenance.
No acquisition or disposal occurred in the period, so there is no integration or acquisition-funding pressure on cash flow.

cp2.weaknesses.text: All debt is one senior secured term loan with no revolving facility, so liquidity rests on cash and operating cash flow and refinancing is concentrated at one date. [Analyst Interpretation]
Customer concentration and the revenue split are not disclosed, so revenue durability cannot be confirmed. [Insufficient Information]

Dividends are paid to the sole shareholder every quarter, the funding source is not documented and the statements are unaudited, which weakens confidence in cash available for debt service. [Analyst Interpretation]

cells.shown: Designs, manufactures and sells fastening and sealing components for industrial equipment, supplied to industrial distributors and original-equipment manufacturers
List prices are reviewed once a year; management states that raw-material cost increases are passed to customers with a lag of one to two quarters [Management Language]
A pass-through lag exposes margin to temporary squeezes when input costs rise
Distributor restocking cycles and original-equipment production schedules
Volumes follow customer inventory and production cycles, which moves revenue with the cycle
Cost of sales consists mainly of steel, elastomer and manufacturing labour
Commodity and labour inputs drive margin resilience
Maintenance of existing plants; no growth capital programme
Capital spending is discretionary-light, which supports cash conversion
Trade receivables, inventories and trade payables
Receivables and inventory absorb cash when volumes grow
